title: Ontario breaks ground on new Ornge and OPP aircraft hangar in Simcoe County
summary: The nearly 100,000-square-foot facility will house four Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) helicopters and multiple fixed-wing aircraft.
body_markdown:
The Ontario government has officially broken ground on the new Ornge and Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) emergency services aircraft hangar at Lake Simcoe Regional Airport.


Backed by a $56.3 million provincial investment, the nearly 100,000-square-foot facility will house Ornge’s two new fixed-wing Special Mission Aircraft, four OPP helicopters and four OPP fixed-wing aircraft, helping strengthen emergency response capabilities and connect more families in rural, Northern and remote communities to emergency services when they need it most.


“As part of our plan to protect Ontario, our government is ensuring Ornge has the resources it needs to deliver fast, life-saving care to patients facing medical emergencies,” said Sylvia Jones, deputy premier and minister of health.


“The state-of-the-art Ornge-OPP hangar will provide a strategically located hub for Ornge’s new high-speed, long-distance Special Mission Aircraft, and ensure timely emergency care is available across Ontario for generations to come.”


The new state-of-the-art hangar will house 10 emergency support aircraft, providing emergency response coverage across the province.


By bringing together air ambulance and policing aviation services at this strategic location, the new hangar will streamline logistics to deploy critical care and law enforcement resources faster, speeding up response times to life-threatening situations such as car accidents, heart attacks and strokes.


Construction on the hangar is set to be completed in winter 2027 and will support approximately 200 good-paying construction jobs in the region.


“When an emergency strikes, every second counts, and our government is committed to ensuring our frontline responders are ready to answer the call,” said solicitor general Michael Kerzner.


“We are making strategic investments to strengthen the OPP’s aviation capabilities and ensuring our frontline heroes have the tools and resources they need to protect Ontario. By bringing the OPP and Ornge together under one roof, we’re strengthening emergency response, supporting faster deployments and helping keep communities safe in every corner of our province.”


OPP Aviation Services operates a fleet of fixed-wing and rotary-wing aircraft that support frontline policing, specialized investigations, search-and-rescue operations, tactical deployments, personnel transportation and emergency response efforts across Ontario.


The shared facility represents a long-term investment in Ontario’s emergency response infrastructure and will support the continued delivery of aviation services across the province.


Through[Your Health: A Plan For Connected and Convenient Care](https://www.ontario.ca/page/your-health-plan-connected-and-convenient-care) , Ontario is building a health-care system that delivers the right care in the right place.


Quick Facts


- Ornge is Ontario’s provincial air ambulance and critical care land ambulance (CCLA) service provider and provides a range of air paramedical services including moving patients between health-care facilities, responding to emergency on-scene incidents, and supporting health care in northern and rural communities.
- Ornge plays a key role in access to care for the province’s northern and rural communities with approximately 98 percent of Ornge’s fixed-wing patient transports originating in northern Ontario.
- Ornge conducts approximately 22,000 air ambulance and land ambulance patient transports per year from nine air bases and five critical care land bases across the province.
- The new hangar and Special Mission Aircraft are in addition to the $[118 million investment announced in 2023](https://news.ontario.ca/en/release/1005508/ontario-connecting-northern-and-rural-communities-to-critical-care) to expand Ornge’s fixed wing fleet to 12 aircraft, including the replacement of the existing eight fixed wing fleet, and purchase of an expanded hangar in Sudbury to house the new aircraft.
- The Ornge Air Ambulance fleet will expand to 14 fixed wing aircraft by 2030, with the first of the new aircraft anticipated to arrive before the end of 2026.
- OPP aircraft are routinely deployed for search-and-rescue missions, missing person investigations, emergency response, surveillance operations, tactical deployments, and transportation of personnel and prisoners.
- OPP aviation assets collectively fly approximately 4,000 hours annually in support of policing and public safety operations across Ontario.


“Co-locating with the Ontario Provincial Police at our new Lake Simcoe Regional Airport base reflects the Government of Ontario’s commitment to collaboration, efficiency, and strong public services,” said Dr. Homer Tien
Ornge president and CEO.


“By sharing infrastructure and resources, we are maximizing value for taxpayers while enhancing our collective ability to deliver critical emergency response capabilities. Together, we share a common goal: ensuring Ontarians receive timely emergency services and care when they need it most. This partnership strengthens our readiness, improves coordination, and reinforces our commitment to keeping communities safe and supported across the region.”


“OPP Aviation Services plays a critical role in supporting frontline policing and emergency response operations across Ontario,” said Thomas Carrique
OPP commissioner.


“This shared facility will enhance our ability to deploy aviation resources efficiently, strengthen collaboration with our emergency service partners at Ornge, and support the safe and effective delivery of services to the communities we serve.”


“The construction of this new Ornge-OPP hangar at Lake Simcoe Regional Airport is an important investment in the safety and well-being of our communities and people across Ontario,” said Doug Downey
MPP for Barrie—Springwater—Oro-Medonte.


“By bringing these critical emergency services together in one strategically located facility, we are strengthening our ability to respond when every second counts, particularly for residents in northern and rural communities. This investment will also create good-paying jobs, support our local economy, and reinforce the importance of Lake Simcoe Regional Airport as a key piece of infrastructure for our region. I’m proud to see our government making investments that deliver meaningful benefits for our communities and help keep Ontarians safe.”


“The Ornge–OPP groundbreaking announcement marks a significant milestone for our entire region and an important step toward saving lives and protecting Ontario,” said Andrea Khanjin MPP for Barrie—Innisfil.


“Our government’s $56.3 million investment will bring life-saving air ambulance and police aviation services together under one roof, helping emergency crews respond faster, reach people in critical need, and deliver emergency care when every second counts. The project will also create approximately 200 good-paying construction jobs in the region, supporting local workers while strengthening the emergency services that protect Barrie-Innisfil and communities across Ontario.”


“As Simcoe County continues to grow, it is important that our emergency services have the infrastructure and resources they need to keep pace,” said Brian Saunderson MPP for Simcoe—Grey.


“This new joint facility at the Lake Simcoe Regional Airport will bring the OPP and Ornge together, strengthening their ability to respond to emergencies and serve communities across Ontario. It is a significant investment in public safety and another important milestone in the continued development of the airport.”


“Today marks an exciting milestone for Simcoe North and an important investment in the safety and security of our communities,” said Jill Dunlop
MPP for Simcoe North.


“This new joint Ornge/OPP Emergency Service Aircraft Facility at Lake Simcoe Regional Airport will strengthen emergency response capabilities, enhance coordination between emergency services, and help ensure that critical resources can be deployed quickly and efficiently when they are needed most. Having this state-of-the-art facility in Simcoe County also reinforces the strategic importance of our regional airport, supports local economic development, and creates opportunities for our community. This is an investment that will benefit not only Simcoe North, but communities across Ontario, and I am proud to see our region playing such an important role in strengthening provincial emergency services.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by the Government of Ontario.*
